title: A Compact Full-Duplex Receiver with Wideband Multi-Domain Hilbert-Transform-Equalization Cancellation Based on Multi-Stage APFs Achieving 65dB SIC Across 120MHz BW
problem: Full-duplex (FD) receiver self-interference cancellation (SIC) techniques face a tradeoff between delay-bandwidth product (DBW), noise figure, and power consumption; most existing cancellers achieve <80MHz cancellation bandwidth with >30dB depth, while frequency-domain equalization-based approaches require power-hungry high-Q filters with noise degradation.
motivation: Full-duplex systems double spectrum efficiency; however, simultaneous TX-RX self-interference cancellation over wide signal bandwidth (toward 320MHz for Wi-Fi 7) is essential to enable next-generation wireless standards.
method: The FD receiver employs multi-domain Hilbert-transform-equalization (HTE) SIC with cascaded low-noise allpass filters (APFs): 1st-order APF in RF canceller tap for flat frequency response, 2nd-order APF with delay-peaking in 2nd tap for extended DBW, achieving 65dB SIC over 120MHz with <10% RF delay variation.
key_novelty: Multi-stage allpass filter architecture with Hilbert-transform equalization enabling wideband self-interference cancellation with superior noise and power efficiency.
contributions: Compact full-duplex receiver with wideband self-interference cancellation
Low-noise (6dB NF) RF cancellation with wide delay range support
primary_theme: Wideband full-duplex receiver with allpass-filter SIC
